title: Ends of the queue
prompt:
A café keeps its waiting customers in a list, first in line first.

Write a function `ends(queue)` that returns a new list with two names: the first person in the queue and the last one. Use indexes, not a loop.

For example, `ends(["Ana", "Ben", "Cleo"])` returns `["Ana", "Cleo"]`. A queue with one person returns that name twice.
hints: The first element is at index 0. What index reaches the last element without knowing the length?
A negative index counts from the end: `queue[-1]` is the last element.

title: Every other day
prompt:
The list `temps` holds a week of midday temperatures, Monday first.

Print three lines, each using one slice of `temps`:

1. the weekend (the last two days),
2. every other day starting with Monday,
3. the whole week backwards.

Then make a copy of `temps` with a slice, set the copy's first element to `0`, and print `temps` again to show the original didn't change.
solution:
temps = [18, 21, 19, 24, 22, 17, 20]

print(temps[-2:])
print(temps[::2])
print(temps[::-1])
copy = temps[:]
copy[0] = 0
print(temps)
hints: A slice is `list[start:stop:step]`, and every part can be left out.
`temps[-2:]` starts two from the end and runs to the end; a step of 2 skips every other element; a step of -1 walks backwards.
`copy = temps[:]` makes a new list, so changing `copy[0]` leaves `temps` alone.
